## Question

<div class="chapter-question">How can we identify patterned differences in model output without immediately assigning them a social cause?</div>

## Why this week belongs here

After treating models as research infrastructure, the course turns them into objects of sociological inquiry. The same measurement and causal-design standards still apply.

## Provisional core readings

- Barrie et al. (2026), §10.6, especially §§10.6.1–10.6.4. [Download chapter PDF](../downloads/readings/ai-and-research-methods-barrie-et-al-2026.pdf). [@BarrieEtAl2026AIResearchMethods]
- Waight et al. (2026), “State Media Control Influences Large Language Models.” [@WaightEtAl2026]
- Buyl et al. (2026), “Large Language Models Reflect the Ideology of Their Creators.” [@BuylEtAl2026]
- Further cases: Kim et al. (2026) and Boelaert et al. (2025). [@KimEtAlConsciousness2026; @BoelaertEtAl2025]

## Planned chapter and class arc

Connect model audits to established audit studies; reconstruct the central papers; distinguish output patterns from explanations about training, culture or alignment; design a factorial audit with predeclared alternatives.

[See the provisional Week 13 Python plan](../python/session13.qmd).
